content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] and recently completed a circuit for a heat controller in a building. I'd like to control a mixing valve with a 3-position control signal. For outputs, I'm using [product_name] expansion modules to prevent potential relay issues from frequent switching. The actuators available online accept 24V AC input, while my module outputs 24V DC. Can anyone suggest how to resolve this incompatibility, or recommend actuators suitable for my setup? Thanks in advance, [user_name]
Hi! In our projects, we often use Sauter actuators, which likely have options suitable for your requirements. [user_name] [url]

Thank you for your recommendation and quick response. It appears that actuators with 24V AC input are more readily available, so I've decided to use external solid state relays as the most practical solution.

Hi [user_name], I've configured a setup where I calculate the average of the PI output, then compare it to the actual value. If there's a change, the control valve opens or closes. Although it's untested, I'm interested to know if [product_name] offers a standard solution for this type of application.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are working on controlling a mixing valve with a [product_name] and accompanying expansion modules, encountering a challenge with actuator input voltage mismatches (24V AC actuators versus the 24V DC outputs of their modules). The conversation discusses difficulties in finding compatible actuators and explores using external relays or alternative actuator brands. There is also some uncertainty about whether [company_name] provides a ready-to-use solution for this scenario.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [company_name] system to directly support widely available actuators with 24V AC input or to offer compatible actuators or standardized solutions for their setup.
